sections.normalized_html: The diagram below shows a carton of orange juice. One-third of the carton is filled with juice, forming a cube. Find the volume of the empty space in the carton.
sections.readable_text:
The diagram below shows a carton of orange juice. One-third of the carton is filled with juice, forming a cube. Find the volume of the empty space in the carton.

[IMG: /graphics/4d1f5ebc0270c6bd0c349bd7bb07c2f2]

sections.normalized_html:
The orange juice in the carton creates a cube. Since the height of the juice is [MATH: 9\,\textrm{cm},] the side length of the cube is also [MATH: 9\,\textrm{cm}.]

The height of [MATH: 9 \: \textrm{cm}] shown in the diagram represents a third of the carton's height. Therefore, the height of the carton is

[MATH: 3 \cdot 9 = 27 \: \textrm{cm}.]

The empty space in the carton is a rectangular prism that is [MATH: 9\:\textrm{cm}] long, [MATH: 9\:\textrm{cm}] wide, and [MATH: 27 - 9 = 18\:\textrm{cm}] high.

We can find the volume [MATH: V] of the rectangular prism using the formula

[MATH: V = lwh,]

where [MATH: l] is the length, [MATH: w] is the width, and [MATH: h] is the height of the solid.

Substituting

[MATH: l=9\,\textrm{cm}, \qquad w=9\,\textrm{cm}, \qquad h=18\,\textrm{cm}]

into the formula, we obtain

[MATH: V = 9 \cdot 9 \cdot 18 = 1\,458\:\textrm{cm}^3.]

Therefore, we conclude that there is [MATH: 1\,458 \: \textrm{cm}^3] of empty space in the carton.
